utterances.text: That's all right. I understand. You were talking about the track record of the 9th and 10th Brigades in your detailed answer to the court. Could you please explain that.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: As I said, I mean, I can't really say much more. It is my view - and not just my view - that those two brigades had a reputation for causing trouble and problems. And after I returned from reporting, after I returned to the 6th Corps, I read through some additional reports and complaints - for example, from Mr. Cibo from the Municipality of Konjic; he protested because those units had beaten up two police officers and they stole a police boat at Jablanica and so on. So this is just to illustrate their reputation. It only confirmed their reputation. It was no news, basically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Tirak, leaving aside the reputation. In military terms, how suitable were the 9th and 10th Brigades for an operation to lift a blockade in a city?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If there's one witness who can't answer that question, given what he's already said about his level of expertise, it is this witness. Your Honours, Mr. Karavelic is coming, I believe, and it may be that he's got the experience and the -- the knowledge to give a meaningful answer to that question. To ask it of this witness, who at his own level of -- of seniority, which he's already given evidence about, in my submission he just shouldn't be asked this question. It goes outside of what he can testify about as an expert, and giving direct evidence he can say absolutely nothing about it, because as he's indicated already, he wasn't there. So if my friend wants to lead expert evidence, he'd have to qualify him as somebody who's able to give an opinion on this topic. If he wants to give evidence -- lead evidence about what he directly knows and says, he can do that. But that question is not permissible, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I submit that this is well within the parameters of the witness's knowledge; however, I will approach it a different way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may try it another way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, earlier on in your evidence, you told the Court about the brigades in the 1st Corps. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told the Court -- well, you named to the Court the brigade -- the 1st Sarajevo Brigade and the 2nd Knightly Brigade. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes, amongst other things, those brigades were in Sarajevo as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Militarily, from your knowledge within the 1st Corps at that time, what did the 1st Sarajevo Brigade and the 2nd Knightly Brigade achieve in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Those are brigades that had the reputation as being the best units in the Sarajevo Corps. They had not only a great deal of success in defending but also in attacking an enemy, and they had always been quoted as examples of well-organised units with brave soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those examples of attacking the enemy, can you tell us more about that, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Well, they had a number of such attack operations, but they became famous by taking the area of Zuc, which is a part of Sarajevo. And when it was conquered, the enemy units were pushed back to Vogosce and so defending Sarajevo from that side was impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the 4th Hrasnica Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Well, I've had more contacts with that brigade during the time that I was at Pazaric. And if I may say so, what I myself and -- well, on the basis of my experience, they had a battalion that could move quickly at any time and engage in combat, and most units at that time were not capable of that, considering the level of training, the skill, and the logistical support and everything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your time in the 1st Corps, not only in Sarajevo with the 6th Mountain Brigade but also in Pazaric, did you know whether the 9th and 10th Brigades had similar military successes?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: No. As far as I can tell, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying you don't know, or are you saying they did not have similar military successes?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I don't know whether they had. And if they had, I would have heard of it, as all the other citizens of BH, because every success of our units was talked about publicly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you heard from Mr. Fazlic that the 9th and 10th Brigades were being brought into the region, what exactly was your reaction?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Pardon me. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must correct you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I must interrupt again. Your Honour, once again, this question here seems to ask what this witness's reaction to that was, and I'd ask what possible relevance that could have to the case Mr. Halilovic is facing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think that this piece of the evidence will go to the reputation of the two brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, if it's a question of the reputation of the brigades, Your Honour, I don't mind that question being asked, even for a third time. But if that's what it's about, it's becoming repetitious. If it's something different, I object to it. I don't want evidence to be led, and I submit it shouldn't be led, of this witness's state of mind and his personal reactions to things. They're very hard matters to deal with in cross-examination because we can't see what they're relevant to. If it's as Your Honour say, I don't object this last time to him eliciting, again, the reputation of those units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that it will go to the reputation of two brigades. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Then I think that you have already -- already have your case established on that by asking so many questions on that aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you started to tell the Court about what Mr. Fazlic said with respect to Grabovica, Mr. Tirak. Can you please continue with that.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Fazlic told me that he had just received information that some crime had happened in Grabovica but at the time of our conversation, he was unable to tell me anything else about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you what kind of crime happened in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: He just said that civilians were harmed, but at that time he did not have any real information as to what it was all about. But as I was getting ready to go and see Mr. Delic straight away when I set off, I had no additional information about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go and see Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I went, first of all, because I was ordered to do so by the deputy commander, to go and inform him about the entire situation and to -- for him to order for those units to be withdrawn straight away from the 6th Corps, from the area of responsibility of the 6th Corps, I mean. And apart from that, there was a whole range of other issues that we wanted to discuss with Mr. Delic of course, matters not pertaining to that particular operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't Mr. Fazlic or Mr. Gusic go and speak to Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: At that time, Mr -- well, the commander of the 6th Corps was absent, and Mr. Fazlic, so to say, was a lot less mobile than I was. I was much quicker. I was younger. And I weighed 30 kilos less, so it was easier for me to -- to go through that physical exertion, because at the time going between Konjic and Visoko was a kind of adventure because there were no true communication lines. You had to go across the hills and ride on horseback, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did you meet Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: At a school at Visoko where he most often stayed when he was in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when that meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I can't say precisely. It was approximately a day after -- or rather, slightly later than 24 hours after I left, after that conversation with Mr. Fazlic. Because at the time, one needed roughly 24 hours to get there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you went to inform him about the entire situation and to -- and for him to order those units to be withdrawn straight away from the 6th Corps. Did you tell Mr. Delic that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What exactly did you say to him?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I told him everything that Mr. Fazlic had told me. And I would just like to stress a whole range of other things that had to do with many other issues in relation to the organisation of the corps or coordination amongst units at the time, so that that conversation took several hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in particular, what did you tell him about Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: If we talk about the fact that the coordination amongst units sometimes was very bad or non-existent in the sense that units moved from the area of one corps to another without sufficient organisation or aimlessly sort of, and then I said that because of that sort of [indiscernible], that because of that sometimes tragic events could take place. Even though, and I'd like to stress this once again, at the time I did not know exactly what had happened. We had received the information that there were some crimes against civilians there, but I could say nothing else, because I had no more specific information myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just want to put on record again- and Your Honours have already ruled so that the ruling will be binding, as with this one as with the last one - but I want to put on record again that Mr. Delic again was withdrawn as a witness. What we now have is another conversation that's being led in exactly the same way. I object to it. I understand what the ruling is likely to be. But I place the objection on record, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll note that. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that sometimes communication was bad or non-existent in the sense that units moved from the area -- from one area of the corps to another without sufficient organisation, which units were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Well, generally speaking, I mean. I'd like to stress that. What I said to Mr. Delic was not only about that specific event that was taking place at the time but also in general, because prior to that it used to happen that individual units would arrive unannounced, without us knowing what was their aim, where they were headed, and what they were supposed to be doing. And when I asked Mr. Fazlic to give me a slightly more detailed account so that I could relate that to Mr. Delic, and he said to me, "Well, that precisely is the problem. We really don't know ourselves everything that's going on and we should know." So basically that was the way he saw this problem. And then I told Mr. Delic that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic -- Mr. Fazlic -- well, you've told the Court that Mr. Fazlic told you about the 9th and 10th Brigades comes into the region; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Not that they were on their way but that they were already there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- well, in respect of that, did you tell -- what did you tell to Mr. Delic in respect of that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I must say that I was rather surprised and I think -- I dare say that I was rather irritated by that, and I said that whoever had brought those units to that area did not know what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who brought those units to that area?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Is my learned friend now attempting to bring this witness's direct evidence in or is he talking about the relayed conversation with Mr. Fazlic to Mr. Delic? Because that question there doesn't seem to be anything to do with the conversation. It seems to be to do with this witness's own thoughts. If so, it's irrelevant and I object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, in my submission, it's a perfectly legitimate question. I'm asking him about his knowledge. As simple as that. He can either say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could my friend please spell out the relevance of this man's knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any, I mean, background information about this man's knowledge on that information?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, I was -- I was going to ask him about that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Try to establish that foundation first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which corps did the 9th and 10th Brigades belong to?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: The 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if the commander of the 1st Corps ordered these troops to go to the region?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke to Mr. Delic, did he tell you that he had asked those troops to go to the region?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: No, he didn't say anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told the Court earlier that Mr. Halilovic was the commander of the operation to deblockade Mostar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, it's not right. He didn't tell anything like that to the Court. He said Mr. Fazlic told him that. And, Your Honour, this is a deliberate -- well, I won't say "deliberate." I withdraw that. This is making the error of blurring what he's told by the witness -- sorry, by the non-witness, Fazlic, with what he says himself. So I object to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'll rephrase that question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told the Court that Mr. Fazlic had told you that Mr. Halilovic was the commander of the operation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes. He was the one who told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told the Court that Mr. Fazlic told you that the 9th and 10th Brigades were brought into the region for that operation; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Mr. Fazlic tell you, if anything, about the command role of the 6th Corps with respect to this operation to deblockade Mostar?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: He told me he had issued orders for those three units of ours that I've mentioned to be involved in the operation. He also said that unfortunately he was not privy to all the details. He struck me as depressed, downbeat, simply because something was happening in the zone of responsibility of our own corps without us being aware of all the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, as the Chief of Staff of the 6th Corps, was your corps responsible for -- in a command function for the operation to deblockade Mostar?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: This is based on what I was told, because I must say this again, I wasn't there physically at the time. So what I was told was that the objective of the command of the 6th Corps was to have those three units resubordinated to the forward command post of the Supreme Command headquarters so that they would then be running all the other units that were involved in the operation. That's at least what I was told.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As Chief of Staff of the 6th Corps, if the 6th Corps was involved in the running of this operation, would you have known about that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: One thing I can say for sure is that the command of the 6th Corps -- if the command of the 6th Corps had planned a large-scale operation like this, I would have been involved without a shadow of a doubt and I wouldn't have been this far away from the scene had this been the case. So one thing I can say for certain is that this operation was not planned by the 6th Corps. Anything else I can only talk about based on what I was told by other persons, but one thing I can tell you from firsthand personal knowledge is that the operation was not planned by the 6th Corps. Had that been the case, I would have been in the know too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, I'm sorry if this is repetition, but just to be clear, did your corps have any command role with respect to the 9th and 10th Brigades when they came into the region?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure that the witness has given any evidence that he was anywhere nearby to form an opinion about that. And perhaps he was, and if so, that evidence can be led. There's a basis for asking that question. But in its current form, I object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's not necessary for this witness to be nearby that area since his position is the Chief of Staff of the 6th Corps --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- which has a zone or area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I -- Your Honours, I think the learned Prosecutors well know -- if I have to cross-examine this out, I will, but I'll put it on record now, in my view, in my submission, it's proper for the Prosecutor to lay the foundation f they refuse to do it, I'll cross-examine on it, as of course I'm entitled to do. And Your Honours will see where he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, could you please answer that question, if you recall it. Did your corps have any command role with respect to the 9th and 10th Brigades when they came to the region?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Based on what my deputy shared with me and based on what I was told by Mr. Fazlic, we were in no way in command of any of those units, nor were we providing any logistical or other support, nor did we have anything to do with any operations that they were carrying out, if indeed any. I am not sure if there were any further contacts between the commands during the operation itself. This is something that I can't confirm for the simple fact that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's get back to the -- to the meeting with Mr. Delic. You told us earlier that you wanted to tell Mr. Delic to order those units, the 9th and 10th Brigades, to go back to Sarajevo. Did you tell Mr. Delic that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Mr. Delic say?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I briefed him, and he provided a diplomatic reply. He said he would look into the whole matter and then take whatever steps were required.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell Mr. Delic about what you learnt with respect to the forward command post in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I've said -- I told him about it; Mr. Fazlic told me that the forward command post was in Jablanica, and he replied that he sort of knew that Mr. Halilovic was in the area but he said he didn't know exactly what he was doing. It didn't strike me as very logical, but that was precisely what he told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't it strike you as logical?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: It doesn't strike me as logical that a commander should not know what his Chief of Staff is doing. It just doesn't strike me as logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, in one of your answers, you've said that -- just to assist you, in line 25 on page 39, you said, "I've said -- I told him about it. Mr. Fazlic told me that the forward command post was in Jablanica." Is that an accurate reflection of what you -- what you have answered from what you recall you answered?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I don't know what that question means, Your Honour. I object to it as a confusing one. Is he asking whether the witness told the truth a few minutes ago when he gave that answer? Your Honours, it --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just trying to clarify the name, I'm sorry. Whether it's Mr. Fazlic or Mr. Delic, as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may ask a question directly to this effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, sorry, do you mean Mr. Fazlic or Mr. Delic in that answer?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic told me that, and then I relayed it to Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, did you at some point find out about the details of what happened in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes. I found out later. I read the report drafted by the chief of security of the 6th Corps, what he wrote about what happened. I didn't take any steps in that respect though. The commander had said that he would notify and inform all those who needed to know, which I assume that he eventually did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to show the witness a document, and it's D157. Do you need the ERN number?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, do you have that document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the English version or the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: The B/C/S version. Both things I can see on the screen are in the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I first saw this document when the investigators showed it to me, but not prior to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which investigator? Just to be clear.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I think it was Mr. Bruno Bernard [phoen], something along these lines. I'm not sure though. That was when I first saw the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes. "Rasim Delic," that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you go to the top of the document and the initial paragraph. Can you just briefly -- well, just read that out for the Court, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Before where it says "Order" you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: "Chief of Staff -- Chief of Staff of the 6th Corps informed me about the decision of the Chief of the Supreme Command Staff in connection with combat operations planned along the Prozor and Mostar axes pursuant to which I hereby order." Is that the only thing you want me to read out, or is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the moment that's fine. Thanks. Well, this is probably redundant, but just to be sure, the Chief of Staff of the 6th Corps, that is yourself; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it's not for the witness to say whether that's right or not right. He can confirm, as he already has, that he was the 6th Corps Chief of Staff. He can't confirm -- at the moment, there's no basis for him confirming anything about this piece of paper. He said that it was shown to him by Bernard Brun or someone sounding similar and that's as far as it goes. And he's not to be asked that question in that form, but he can confirm, of course, that he was the 6th Corps Chief of Staff. The Defence isn't going to challenge that -- that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the witness said that he first saw this document when the investigators showed it to -- to this witness. But here in the document it says "the 6th Corps Chief of Staff has informed Mr. Delic about certain matters," so there's a problem there. You may ask a question to clarify it, this problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, Mr. Tirak: Do the contents of this document reflect any part of your conversation with Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I object --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any conversation that you told the Court about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I want -- I object to that. It's not for this witness to say whether this document reflects the conversation that he had or not, unless he's told something about the order at a later time by Mr. Delic or it's otherwise confirmed as being connected with him. What he can legitimately say is, "I told Mr. Delic certain things, he told me certain things." But unless he saw the making of this document or had something to do with it, he just can't ask. He can't be asked whether that is connected in any way with that conversation. As I've said -- I want it to be clear so that no one is in any doubt, the Defence has got the gravest concerns about this document and provenance and we don't accept it as genuine, frankly, at this stage. There's going to be challenges to it. So that's why I'm objecting in the detail that I am. It's not for fun or to make Mr. Sachdeva's day more difficult than it otherwise should be. It's because of that issue. And that's why I'm being very precise about it. And that's why I object to this witness being asked to comment on whether that document matches what he told Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the answer to this witness may also be helpful to your case on that, you know. And -- Mr. Sachdeva, you may put the first line of this document into a question and put it to this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, did you inform Mr. Delic about the decision of the Chief of the -- about planned combat operations towards Prozor and Mostar in your conversation with Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, with respect, that's got to be put accurately. That's left out a chunk of what's in that sentence. If my friend wants to do that, he's got to put the whole sentence. And leaving that part out really gives away what they're worried about, with respect. But I'll limit my objection to -- that he's got to put the whole thing properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But I believe that everything is almost there, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it's -- Your Honours, the bit that I was concerned about being left out was -- the line says: "The 6th Corps Chief of Staff has my friend me about," and then my friend left out this bit: "the decision of the Chief of Staff -- Chief of Supreme Command Staff."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In other words, it's the Halilovic bit that got left out. And that's what my friend didn't want to ask, apparently. I submit that if he wants to ask that question, he should put the whole thing fairly and in context, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since there's a Defence objection, well, Mr. Sachdeva, would you please do according to what the Defence said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, did you inform Mr. Delic about the decision of the Chief of the Supreme Command Staff regarding planned combat operations -- actions towards Prozor and Mostar.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I informed Mr. Delic about the situation as it was at the time, based on what Mr. Fazlic had told me. The conversation took three hours, and I'm not sure why Mr. Delic chose to speak only about this particular segment. I really have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your conversation with Mr. Delic, you say it took three hours.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I can't say exactly. Between two and three hours. It was a long one, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this segment in this document part of your conversation with Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Once again, I object. That was the original objection. What I submit the Prosecutor is trying to do here is to get this witness to validate a suspect document by his memory. Now, we've got no objection to him saying what he told the witness, and he -- he has done that. But if they want it again, I don't object to that. But to attempt to validate this document is not legitimate. And I -- I object to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. -- Mr. Tirak has already given evidence about the conversation he had with Mr. Delic and he's been quite detailed in that evidence. Now, I'm simply asking him whether the material in this document, leaving aside whether it's authentic or -- or anything else, reflects, either in part or in totality, that conversation with Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, this question is allowed. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What this document says: "In part also reflects what I had told him." But again I must say it includes something that he got from another source, because at the time we spoke the only thing I knew was that units from Sarajevo had committed some sort of a crime in Grabovica. At the time, I was not aware of the fact that it had been the 9th Mountain Brigade, nor was I in a position tell him about it. He must have found out from a different source. Let me make this clear. At that time, I had no idea what unit it was that had committed the crimes. I only told him that crimes had been committed in Grabovica, but I could not talk about the exact extent of those crimes or indeed who the perpetrators had been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you ask Mr. Delic for the 9th and 10th Brigades to be sent back to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Because I believed that those units were not able to contribute much to any offensive operations. It wasn't only my opinion. It was shared by all the members of the 6th Corps command who were there. They could only cause trouble, and that's why we asked for those units to be withdrawn from the area of responsibility of the 6th Corps a.s.a.p. That was why I requested their urgent withdrawal. The news of this crime that had taken place only reinforced me in this request.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps this is the time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And we will take a longer break, since the Defence will have an opportunity to talk to the next witness. And we'll resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sachdeva. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, I want to ask you, as I said earlier, some questions about the Prozor Independent Battalion. Now, you told the Court that you -- you went to meet the battalion in -- sometime in July 1993. Where did you meet with them?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: It was three villages in that region: Scipe, Here, and Kute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of that battalion?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I can't remember the name exactly, but I know we all used to call him Buza, but I can't really remember what his real name was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, who comprised the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: At that time, the Independent Battalion Prozor was made up of peasants from those three villages, about 50 of them, and up to 100 people who were actually refugees from Prozor and the surrounding settlements, and that's where they found their refuge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did these villagers and refugees have any military experience?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: No. They were farmers, people who were mostly farmers and apart from doing their military service, I don't suppose they've had any other military experience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was this situation, in that the Prozor Independent Battalion was made up of persons without military experience, was this situation mirrored throughout the 6th Corps

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Of course not just throughout the 6th Corps but in the BH army in general there has always been a shortage of people with military experience, but in other units we did have superiors and other soldiers with some military experience. Some of them even had considerable military experience. It was just in that unit that there was nobody at all who would have had any military experience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you say that the situation with respect to the Prozor Independent Battalion was a unique situation with respect to the other units in the corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: If by that you mean that there were no people with any military experience there, yes. Other units had a certain number of people with military experience, but there was nobody like that in that particular unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you know of a -- a place called Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I've heard of that place after those tragic events. Prior to that, I must admit I'd never heard of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What tragic events are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: What I found out later, that a certain number of people had come to grief there. That's what I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you find out about this?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I'm unable to tell you precisely, but sometime in the course of October, but I can't tell you exactly on what day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "come to grief," what -- what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Since I'm not a lawyer, I don't know what a legal definition would be, but people there had been killed in a way which is inappropriate at any time, and that includes war operations as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know or were you told who was responsible for this incident?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I must say that when I found out about that incident, I was quite surprised because in the course of my visit to that unit, those people gave me the impression of being rather peaceful, if I may say that. They did not look like people who were capable of doing a thing like that. There were people that tended to think about their cattle, about farming a lot more than about military matters, and they did not come across as people who were capable of doing something like that. When I found out about it, I really wanted to find out exactly what had happened, but relatively soon afterwards I actually left the 6th Corps, so unfortunately I never got the opportunity what exactly happened there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told the Court that 100 of these persons who made up the Prozor Independent Battalion were refugees from Prozor.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes, or from the surrounding areas. Perhaps not just Prozor itself but from the surrounding area as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, is there any significance of that fact with respect to what you heard happened in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this seems to be an attempt to get the witness to speculate as to who might be guilty of committing certain acts at Uzdol. To say as a fact that somebody was a refugee got something to do with what might have happened is speculative even of a witness who knew something about the case. But this witness has said he didn't find out anything until October, so that not only was it an impermissible question for a witness who knew something, but it's wrong to ask this witness this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we haven't come to the evidence in Uzdol and who committed the crime has not been introduced, you know, in our proceedings, so you might come too fast to that point, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: One second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told the Court that people had been -- from what you heard, people had been killed in an inappropriate way. Who were killed?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: What I heard was that the inhabitants of that village had been killed, but I must say that after 12 years I can't tell you specifically, who exactly, and how many they were and all that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who did the killings?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, pardon me, Witness. Again, I object to that. This now seems to be an attempt to get crime-base evidence in from someone who didn't know anything about it for a month. Your Honours, I object. If it be proved of course that he has some basis for knowing, then I won't object. For example, if he was there or if he participated in the investigation in some way, I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that must be some, you know, hearsay evidence because the witness already testified that he heard those incidents much later, so there's some hearsay evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So in this aspect, we'll allow the question to go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As long as -- Your Honour, may I just say -- it's true and I'm bound by Your Honours' ruling, but at least we ought to know where the hearsay came from. It's hard for -- hard to see what use it could be otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, could you please answer the question. Do you know who did the killing?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: No, who exactly, I don't know. If I knew, well, I would have said it a long time ago and I would have asked for the actually perpetrators to be punished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you would have asked for the actual perpetrators to be punished, at that time was the 6th Corps responsible for the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the 6th Corps responsible for the Prozor Independent Battalion when Mr. Fazlic ordered the Prozor Independent Battalion to be part of the operation to liberate Mostar?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: At that juncture all those three units were subject to the forward command post, so at the time the 6th Corps was not in charge of them. And on the basis of what I found out from my colleagues, it was not just that they were not formally in charge but in terms of substance as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to leave the topic of the Prozor Independent Battalion and ask you a few more questions about the 9th and 10th Brigades, if I may. Given what you've told the Court about the other brigades of the 1st Corps and their military successes, and given what you've told the Court additionally about the reputation of the 9th and 10th Brigades of the 1st Corps, were you told at any time why the 9th and 10th Brigades were brought to the region for this operation?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I've already told you when I heard that those units were included in the operation and the reason for their coming was to participate in the operation aimed at lifting the blockade of Mostar. As to why those units were chosen and not some other units, well, that's something I can't tell you at any rate. Had I been in a position to choose, it is certain that I wouldn't have selected those units and I would have chosen some other units. But as to why they were selected, I must say I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told or do you know who selected those units for the operation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, again it's one of those double questions. First of all, the witness could be asked was he told, and just as a courtesy to the Defence, he might be asked who he was told by, so that we know, but not to put the two questions together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You might have it -- split it, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told who selected those units for the operation?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I never found out about it. All I can say is that it is certain that the decision for those two units to be participating in that operation certainly did not originate in the 6th Corps. Otherwise, I would have known about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, pardon me for intervening here. I'm told by the Bosnian speakers at the table that the witness actually said "no" as the first word there and it's come out as "yes." I wonder if we could just clarify with the interpreters or the translators what the situation is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The translators acoustically heard "da," but I it may well be that it's a no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm no expert so it better be clarified. I'm not going to say anyone was wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe the witness himself is the best person to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tirak, when I asked you who selected those units for the operation, the transcript reads: "Yes." What is your answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: No, I said I did not know who actually selected those two units. I also said that if I had been in a position to choose, I certainly would not have selected those two units. And finally, I also said something that I was certain about was that certainly no one from the 6th Corps invited those two units to participate in that or any other operation, because I would have known about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Morrissey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Tirak. You were the Chief of Staff of the 6th Corps, is that correct, in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can tell this Tribunal one thing about Chiefs of Staff, and that is that Chiefs of Staff cannot issue combat orders unless they're specifically authorised to do so by their commander; is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Now, you've given evidence about what you were told by Mr. Bahrudin Fazlic. Now, I just want to be clear about a couple of things. First of all, Bahrudin Fazlic was the deputy commander of the 6th Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And his nickname was Braco, B-r-a-c-o; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, at no time were you shown any document appointing Sefer Halilovic to command any operation; is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: No. If you mean an order, I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was precisely what I meant. Now, I just wanted to ask you some questions about the 9th and 10th Brigades. Your position in -- in Sarajevo was that you joined the struggle and you joined the 6th Mountain Brigade on its part of the front line within Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, you participated in combat with that brigade until the end of 1992, at which time you were transferred to other duties; is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other duties took you to be in command of a logistics base in Pazaric located outside of Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Pazaric was an area which was covered by these -- it was in the area of responsibility of the 1st Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it also lay on the other side of the tunnel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes. At the time when I was there, the tunnel did not exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And communications at that time between Pazaric and -- and the Chief of the -- or sorry, the command post of the 1st Corps were quite difficult; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: No more and no less than on a regular basis normally during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it was easier to move from Pazaric to Sarajevo once the tunnel was built, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes, but even before the tunnel, I used to go -- come and go very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And were you under fire when you came and went from time to time?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Now, I've got a question for you about the 1st -- the 4th Brigade at Hrasnica. You gave evidence about that brigade earlier on. Was that brigade, the 4th Brigade, commanded by an individual named Fikret Prevljak?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Fikret Prevljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And your indication was that that unit had a -- a mobile battalion or a battalion that was able to be deployed away from its -- from the area of operations of that brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes. And they did so several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know -- there's been evidence about this in this court already. Did you know that Fikret Prevljak refused even to lend any trucks to Sefer Halilovic in September of 1993 during the course of combat operations or just before combat operations in the Herzegovina area? Did you know that fact?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Your -- your -- I have to ask you some questions about your military experience now, apart from fighting. In terms of training for -- for military staffing and -- and similar, you achieved the rank of captain in the JNA. But could I ask you: Did you go through the normal military schools and military training to get to that rank of captain?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I finished the reserve officer's school and the rank of captain was something I got on the basis of my contract, considering my duties and my other -- and I don't have any other military training in practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed at the time when you joined the struggle in Sarajevo, the truth was that to your perception the town was in grave danger of falling to the attacking Army of the Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you fought in your area of town but you are also aware that the 9th and 10th Brigade had important parts of the front line to defend themselves; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Certainly. By all means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in terms of the 9th Brigade, you were aware that most of the soldiers in that brigade defended the lines they had to defend bravely and loyally; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Certainly, since they managed to defend it, it means they must have defended it loyally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And your perception was that although you heard some bad rumours about Ramiz Delalic, Celo, and certain people surrounding him, most of the soldiers in the 9th Brigade were just good young men from Sarajevo who were fighting to save their city; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I think that you may have -- might have misinterpreted my words. Most people around him were not good guys, and those who were on the front lines and were defending the city were not around him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, perhaps we're thunderously agreeing and perhaps we're not. I'll just have to make sure we -- we understand each other there. Do you agree that most of -- I'll just take it step by step because I'm a bit slow sometimes. Do you agree that most of the soldiers in the 9th Brigade were just decent young men defending their city?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I'm certain of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And as to those who were not good people, you have given evidence here about the stories that you heard from other people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with respect to Ramiz Delalic, you never met him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes -- oh, no.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speaker corrects himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pardon me. We've just had a bit of a -- trouble there. The answer is you never met him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I don't think I've ever met him. Perhaps in passing, but I don't think I've ever met him or talked to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. All right. Now, the time at which you were in Sarajevo came to an end at the end of 1992, but when you were at Pazaric, you used to come back in from time to time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes, very often, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But late in May and early in June, you became -- the 6th Corps was founded and you were invited to come along and join that 6th Corps as the Chief of Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And thereafter you were based in Konjic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's fair to say, isn't it, that the situation that you and those in -- at the senior levels of the 6th Corps had to face was one of absolute chaos which you had to try and organise in the new corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so that the Tribunal understands what happened with the 6th Corps, the 4th Corps used to cover a large area from Mostar right up towards Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Almost as far as, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And just doing the best you can, can you remember where the 4th Corps used to reach to and where the border between the 4th and the 1st Corps used to be?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: The area under the 1st Corps ended in the Turcin area, and the area of the 4th Corps began at Bradina. It's a mountain pass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, at the time when the hostilities with the HVO began, it soon turned out that the 4th Corps was split by the HVO cutting certain roads; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes, splitting into many sections, many parts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. So the 6th Corps had the -- when the 6th Corps was brought into being, it had the role of collecting all of these units and bringing some sort of central organisation to those units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it's the fact, isn't it, that you had the role of going out onto the terrain and meeting with these units and attempting to bring them into the system of command and control of the 6th Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Precisely. It wasn't only me. The same applied to all other members of the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. But you particularly had -- had the role of travelling around like that and being out on the terrain and getting to know the local commanders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in July of 1993, you became aware that there was a big battle going on in the area of Mount Igman; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did some parts of your corps, the 6th Corps, go to Mount Igman to fight and to help stop the Serbian -- the Republika Srpska offensive in that area?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And at that time, did it come to your knowledge that elements of the 9th and 10th Brigade were also sent out of Sarajevo to fight on Igman to stop that advance of the Army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I don't know about the specific units, but I know many units left Sarajevo in a bid to stop that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if other witnesses give evidence in this court that the 9th and 10th -- or that parts of the 9th and 10th Brigade indeed were taken out to Sarajevo -- out to Igman, then you wouldn't dispute that evidence, would you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Sachdeva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I don't see how the witness can answer that question. It's purely speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that you wouldn't dispute that evidence means that the witness is not in the position to say something contrary to that fact, so there's no problem with that. There must be a lot of reasons for that. I believe this question is allowed. Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that the witness understands it, I'll put it again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If other witnesses give evidence that -- that the elements of the 9th and 10th Brigade did go to Igman to fight, you wouldn't dispute that, would you?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Why would I dispute that? I myself didn't know about it, but others may know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I just want to get a sense of -- did you go back to Sarajevo on -- on any occasions once you took up these busy duties as Chief of Staff of the 6th Corps in -- and the time period I'm asking about here is June, July, August, September. So in those months, did you go back to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: In those months, I only went back once, as far as I can remember. As I said, I was busy trying to bring order to those units that had been torn apart, but I simply didn't have a lot of time to go back to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not being critical about that. I just wanted to know the fact. And therefore, as to what units were and were not available to be taken down to Herzegovina out of the 1st Corps, you just have no idea what the situation was in Sarajevo in the 4th Corps late in August and early in September; is that accurate? Sorry, I've misspoken there. I've said "the 4th Corps." I'll stop that question and I'll ask it again and I'll ask it correctly instead. As far as which units were available to be taken out of the area of the 1st Corps and down to fight in Herzegovina, you yourself cannot comment on who was and was not available in the 1st Corps at that time; namely, late August, early September; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Quite correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, it's -- I withdraw that. I'll -- Would you excuse me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Pardon me. It's a false alarm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for that. Now, the village of Grabovica was originally in the zone of responsibility -- area of responsibility of the 4th Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Formally speaking, it never was, because the zone of responsibility, area of responsibility of the 4th Corps stretched as far as Jablanica, which is some way to the north of the village of Grabovica, but at that time there were no units of the 4th Corps there. Conditionally speaking, we were the ones who covered the area, sent out patrols, and did reconnaissance, and so on and so forth. Formally speaking, at least based on those orders that I had inspected, the area of responsibility of the 6th Corps ended at Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, I've got two questions about that. The first one is: Did you ever see a document that was issued by Rasim Delic, commander of the Bosnian army, on the 29th of August of 1993, which was the conclusions from a meeting of corps commanders at Zenica? Did you ever see that document?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: No, I'd never seen that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, were you aware of whether or not at Zenica it was ordered by Commander Delic that the line of demarcation between the 4th and 6th Corps was drawn just to the south of the village of Grabovica? Is that something you became aware of or not? And I mean formally drawn, not just as a matter of de facto reality.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: As I have already said, I've never seen that order; therefore, I was not aware of any of that. Nor did anyone at the 6th Corps staff take this into account. We didn't really consider what the line of demarcation was in a formal sense. You must realise how simple it is to draw a line on a map. In practice, however, it's a lot more complicated than just that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I have no doubt that's correct. But would you agree with this proposition: Whatever the formal position might be, the 6th Corps assumed de facto responsibility for the village of Grabovica, sending patrols there and generally protecting it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's beyond dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, I was going to ask counsel to provide a specific time period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's a legitimate request.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think it is too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The learned Prosecutor has just asked that we specify the time period there. And I'm talking now about the time period in early September of 1993. And I take it -- well, that's the time period I'm asking about. And in early September of 1993, that was the situation, wasn't it, that the 6th Corps had assumed de facto responsibility for the village of Grabovica? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Throughout my time with the 6th Corps, as there were no other units, we practically did our best to cover the area in order to prevent surprise attacks from the enemy by that direction, so every now and then we would go to the area and send patrols out. But no units of the 6th Corps before ever actually stationed at Grabovica itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you yourself go to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I went there once. It was about a month after I'd been assigned to the 6th Corps, when people from the command of the 44th Brigade showed me around, showed me where the lines were, where our positions were and those of the enemy. I passed the village, but I did not enter the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- so that was in July approximately; is that an accurate -- you won't have a date, I know, but was that approximately in July?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I'd really be hard put to say. It's possible. And in late July as well. It's been 12 years, and I am not very good at timing these events, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you've indicated that there were two units in the -- in the Herzegovina area who you say were not under the control -- or not in the line of control and command of the 6th Corps. You named them as the Black Swans, on the one hand, and Zulfikar's unit, on the other. But apart from those units, you had a responsibility as Chief of Staff of the 6th Corps to know broadly speaking whereabouts the other units in that area were based; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I apologise, but I'd like a clarification as to the units of which corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, if you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I have no difficulty with that, if it's a problem. The 6th Corps. It's in his corps, which I thought I was asking about. By my friend is entitled to the clarification.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, Witness. We have to ask that question again. The question is this: You had a responsibility as Chief of Staff of the 6th Corps to know broadly speaking whereabouts your units were based; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you came to know that a small unit called Cedo's Wolves, sometimes also called the Igman Wolves, were based right smack in Grabovica on the left bank; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I don't know which specific period of time you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have in mind the last two weeks of August and the first week of September 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: At that time, I spent most of my time around Fojnica and Vakuf. This was something that my deputy and Mr. Fazlic dealt with. On account of my other duties in the other half of our area of responsibility, I spent most of my time elsewhere. At times I was not fully informed. Whenever I came, they would brief me, but I must admit my recollection of specific details is not really very good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you don't dispute then that Cedo's Wolves were in fact billeted right smack in the middle of that village of Grabovica in the administration building, in fact, of the hydroelectric company some three weeks before the tragedy in -- at Grabovica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: The hydroelectric company is not right in the middle of Grabovica, if that's what you mean. If that's where they were, then they can't have been in the village of Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you know whether they were there or not?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Handzar Division? Were they accommodated in a house on the right bank of the Neretva in the first week of September and before the arrival of the Sarajevo troops?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I have already told you, I'm not sure about that period, which units came or went. Mr. Fazlic told me that he hadn't been clear about these things himself, which was one of the reasons I went to see Mr. Delic, to lodge a protest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to Mr. Delic a bit later on. But is your -- is your evidence to this Tribunal this: That in that three-week period that I've asked you about, you've got no idea whether these units were billeted in Grabovica or not? And by "these units," I mean the Handzar and Cedo's Wolves. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes. At that time - I can't emphasise this sufficiently - I was not physically present in the area, which is why I know precious little about what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you'll recall the discussion between the Prosecutor and the Court earlier on. You were Chief of Staff of this whole area and you had to receive reports, didn't you, about this topic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: That's correct. But as I've already explained, I was dealing more with organisational matters, coordination, logistics, that sort of thing. I left the military aspects -- or rather, that's what the agreement was within the corps, to the commander and his deputy. That's how it worked throughout my time there. They covered the military aspect, and I covered the other aspect. This was necessary to cover for my lack of familiarity with military issues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. Okay. Very well. Now, the situation facing the 6th Corps in August of 1993 was that the 6th Corps had to cover a very long front line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had to cover a front line -- I'm really only going to ask you questions about the HVO part of that front line now. But you had to cover a front line that stretched from Gornji Vakuf, in the north, right down to Dreznica, in the south; is that the fact?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes, and what's more, the area towards Bileticevo, towards the positions of the units of the Army of Republika Srpska that were in Eastern Herzegovina, and also we had within our composition the Visoko Brigade and we had to cover the area of responsibility facing both the HVO and the Republika Srpska. The conclusion is our area of responsibility was in fact far greater than the one you have just described.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. But the fact is that on the HVO front line, which I've -- do you agree with me that the HVO line went from Gornji Vakuf, in the north, down to Dreznica, in the south?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you gave evidence here that the 6th Corps had no involvement in the planning of the operation to deblock Mostar. Do you stand by that evidence or not?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I stand by the fact that the staff of the 6th Corps planned no such operation. Whether anyone was called in Jablanica, the people who were there, whether any suggestions were made on their part, is something I don't know about. What I am 100 per cent certain about, however, is that no such operation was ever planned by the staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, that's right. And, of course, the staff would know if -- if -- if any such operation was planned, you would know about that, wouldn't you? Because you were the Chief of Staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Had the staff planned this operation, we would have made proposals as to which units were to be brought in and when the attack was to commence. Seeing as we never did this, that means we weren't planning an operation. The simple truth is at the time we didn't have the resources that this would have required. Once the deputy commanders were informed - although I wasn't there myself, but this is what I assume - they must have --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... just let me stop you there, please. I'm not concerned about what you assumed. But I am concerned by this: Did you go to a meeting at Dobro Polje on the 5th of September yourself?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Dobro Polje? No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't comment on any planning discussions that took place at that particular meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: That's certainly true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you, as Chief of Staff, according to you were told nothing about any planning meeting that took place at Dobro Polje; is that correct?, on the 5th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Just excuse me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness -- I'm going to show you a document now. This is 65 ter number D105. Its ERN number is DD00-- sorry, I'll start again, DD000423. We think it's -- the next exhibit is MFI294. Could the witness please be shown that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's about to be shown to you now is an order, and I want to ask for your comment on this order. All right. Do you have in front of you now in Bosnian -- the Bosnian language an order which purports to be sent to the 6th Corps command and originates from commander of the SVK, Rasim Delic? Have you got that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: While the witness is looking at that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm just wondering now. There's five minutes to go. I just wanted to show the witness the map. But really there's going to be a shortage of time about that, and that's really the next topic I want to move to now. Rather than -- I'll ask the witness a couple of questions about this document, but then I might have to stop, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now, Mr. Tirak, do you -- have you read that order that's in front of you there?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And do you see that that's an order from Rasim Delic to your corps, of which you were the Chief of Staff, to launch particularly fierce attacks along a particular axis and to attempt to link up to the 4th Corps command? Do you see those instructions given there?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you make a plan to put that into being pursuant to Commander Delic's order?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: If this is the order which arrived on the 30th of June, then I can tell you that we were facing great difficulties at that time trying to liberate the road between Konjic and Jablanica and establish some sort of control in the Neretva River Valley. Therefore, we were using all the available forces in that area. That's as long as we're talking about the order which arrived on the 6th -- on the 30th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't think we're talking about the same order here. I'm a bit concerned about that. Do you see at the top of your order there that it's dated Sarajevo 2nd of July?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: 2nd of July, yes. But it says "Pursuant to order of the 30th of June."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Further down. If you can see that. Maybe you should have a look. At that time, the corps was - how should I put it? - still consolidating, and the best we could do at the time was launch offensives and link the units up and to clear the road between Konjic and Jablanica and secure to the extent that we could the Neretva River Valley. Even if we were so inclined, there was no way we could have got there physically, if that's the period of time you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the period of time I have in mind is the period that is on the order here, but in any event, is your answer to my -- is your position about all of this that at this time, that is, late in June and early in July, you did receive an order from Rasim Delic but you weren't in a position to draft a detailed plan? Is that effectively what you say about that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But given your answers there, I take it you agree that your corps certainly received this document and knew about it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I must say that throughout my time there we received a great deal of orders, some of which were quite outlandish. This was the main reason I complained to Rasim Delic. It was quite obvious that the people at the Supreme Command headquarters sometimes did not have truthful or reliable information and they issued orders as an alibi. It was clear to everyone at the time, to the company and to the corps as well, that there was not a cat's chance in hell of anything like this actually being put into effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to explain that a little bit further, you mean that people sometimes issued orders that they knew that they had no chance of having carried out? In order to look as if they were doing something effectively?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I can't say what they knew and what they didn't know, but these decisions or orders were some sort of an alibi and I failed to fathom the purpose behind that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. But when you say "some sort of an alibi," that's what I'm asking about now. You're saying that you received as the -- as the Chief of Staff of 6th Corps you saw many orders coming out of the SVK and the Main Staff in Sarajevo, and you indicated that you thought that some of those orders were being put forward just as an alibi almost. And I want to ask you about that. What you mean, I take it, is that people would issue orders from Sarajevo knowing full well they couldn't be carried out but creating the appearance that they were active and issuing orders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: I can't say what the purpose was behind them doing this, whether perhaps they wanted, as you say, to create the appearance of doing something or perhaps encourage the people of the 4th Corps to endure the situation, to make it look like something was actually being done, but it is true that on a number of occasions we received orders that were strange, to say the least. As for the purpose, one thing I can say is that I complained to Mr. Delic about these orders as well. The reply I got was that I should stay out of it, this was something I didn't understand, this was a political matter and to be understood in that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the final question therefore is that: To your observation, just because an order gets issued doesn't mean it's going to have any effect whatsoever on the people it's issued to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD TIRAK
utterances.text: Unfortunately this was often the case in the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, we have to stop here and you have to stay in The Hague for another day. As I did to other witnesses, that during your stay in The Hague you are still under the oath, so do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. So the hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour -- sorry, pardon me. There's just one matter I raise. I apologise for doing this late. In fact, I'll do it tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe the -- maybe tomorrow afternoon would be the best opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 31st day of March, 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.05 p.m.,
